title: Reclaim lock screen keyboard focus after resume from suspend
author: jonathan-downs
body:
## Summary

- The lock screen's password field only regrabs keyboard focus when `inputEnabled` toggles or when the user clicks/moves the pointer on the lock surface (`LockView`'s `wakeRequested`). A real suspend/resume does neither: the lock was already active before the machine slept, so `inputEnabled` never changes, and there's no pointer activity on resume. The surface comes back with no focused input, so nothing you type registers until you click the screen.
- Adds `omarchy-resume-focus-monitor.service`, a systemd user service mirroring the existing `omarchy-sleep-lock.service`, running `bin/omarchy-system-resume-monitor`. It watches logind's `PrepareForSleep` signal for the resume case (`boolean false`) and calls a new `lock` IPC verb, `resume()`, on each occurrence.
- `lock/Service.qml`'s `resume()` IPC handler calls a new `handleSystemResume()` that reuses `runWake()` and bumps a new `resumeSignal` property, wired into `LockView` so it reclaims focus the same way the click handler already does.

**Note on design:** my first pass ran the monitor as a plain QML `Process` owned by `Service.qml` instead of a systemd service. Testing on real hardware caught a real leak in that approach: when Quickshell itself is torn down (a shell restart, a crash-and-relaunch), the `Process`'s own child can be killed abruptly enough that its coproc'd `dbus-monitor` grandchild is orphaned rather than reaped, reparenting to the user's systemd instance and leaking a live system-bus connection indefinitely. Reproduced across multiple shell restarts before fixing it. The systemd-service approach here avoids that entirely: the whole unit's cgroup (dbus-monitor included) is torn down together regardless of how the service itself exits, matching the existing pre-sleep monitor's own approach for the same reason.

## Related

Encountered while investigating a report involving a suspend/resume-specific numpad quirk on the lock screen (separate root cause, not addressed here). This PR only covers the confirmed, reproducible focus issue. It touches the same file as a few other open suspend/resume + lock-screen issues, so linking for context in case of overlapping work:

- #11820
- #12140
- #11744

## Test plan

- [x] `./test/cli` - all passing
- [x] `./test/shell` - all passing except 5 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change and reproducible on a clean checkout (`config-test.sh`, `locate-test.sh`, `omarchy-kernel-migration-test.sh`, `snapper-test.sh`, `unowned-system-paths-test.sh`)
- [x] New `test/shell.d/resume-monitor-test.sh`: verifies the monitor calls `omarchy-shell lock resume` once per resume event while ignoring sleep events, cleans up its `dbus-monitor` producer when the pipeline itself is killed directly (bypassing systemd, to prove the script doesn't rely on systemd alone), and that `--consume` parses events correctly from stdin. Ran 5x in a loop with no leaked processes.
- [x] New assertions in `test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh` for the service file's `ExecStart` path, environment/ordering conditions, `Restart=always`, and that first-run enables it
- [x] Verified locally on real hardware via a plugin clone of `lock` plus the real systemd service: lid-close suspend/resume no longer requires a click before the password field accepts input, and confirmed zero leaked `dbus-monitor` processes across multiple shell restarts and service (re)starts
